name: Week 23 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Lateral Raise + Incline Overhead Tri Ext)
description:
Push day, spotlights cycle to the two shoulder/arm isolations — lateral raise and the incline overhead triceps extension.

The cable block rotates its order again, per the standing rule: this week the **tri extension leads** and the straight-arm pulldown moves off the tail entirely. Last week proved the difficulty was position, not load — so no lift should sit dead-last two weeks running.

Push press and incline DB hold. Dips keep their tempo. The floor's been rising; let it.

dayOverview.theme: Spotlights rotate to the lateral raise and the incline overhead triceps extension — the two isolations that have been running on autopilot and can take a real cue pass. Cable block order rotates again (tri ext leads, straight-arm off the tail). Push press and incline DB hold at settled loads; dips hold bodyweight with the tempo lever.

spotlights.why: It's been 'fine' at 15 for weeks with a near-failure option you rarely need, which is exactly the profile of a lift that's quietly ready for a form pass rather than a number. You said yourself you could go slower. The side delt is a small muscle that rewards a clean line and constant tension far more than load — so the spotlight is the slow lift, the lead-with-the-elbow cue, and keeping the traps quiet so the delt actually does the work instead of the shrug stealing it.

This one just told you something useful by accident — it 'got much harder' the moment it ran last in the cable block. That makes it a good spotlight now that it's back at the front: with the fatigue variable removed, you can actually judge the movement itself. The whole point of the incline-overhead position is the deep stretch on the long head of the triceps, and the cue that matters is a fixed elbow — only the forearm moves. Drill that while it's fresh.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Push spotlights rotate: W21 dips + farmer carry · W22 push press + straight-arm pulldown · W23 lateral raise + incline overhead tri ext (current) · W24 back to incline DB + Kinesis fly. Cable-block ORDER rotates weekly: W22 straight-arm first → W23 tri ext first → W24 cable lat raise first.
watchpoints: **Cable block order ROTATES again: tri ext FIRST, then straight-arm, cable lat raise last.** No lift sits dead-last two weeks running — that's the standing rule. Straight-arm holds 120 in the middle slot.
**🔆 Lateral raise: the spotlight is the SLOW lift** 🔥. Lead with the elbow, traps quiet, constant tension. You said you could go slower — do. 15 stays; tempo is the lever.
**🔆 Incline overhead tri ext: fixed elbow, deep stretch** 🔥. Only the forearm moves. Now that it's back at the front, judge the movement, not the fatigue.
**Push press holds 45** 🛑 — 'could do more in the end' last week. Cash that through a slower eccentric or a pause, not more load. The pack-down is the cap.
**Incline DB holds 50** 🛑 — 55 is available whenever the pack-down survives all 12 reps. You put a 2s eccentric on it voluntarily last week; keep that.
**Dips hold bodyweight, tempo is the lever** 🛑. Watch the palms — pressure showed up last week; if it persists it's a hand-position thing on the bars, not load.
**Farmer carry holds 50lb, 3 walks** — it's a nothingburger now, which is the point. No number needed.
**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure last set OK — lateral raise, cable lat raise, tri ext. 🛑 keep it shy — push press, incline DB, dips, Kinesis fly, straight-arm pulldown, farmer carry.
**Cool-down is not optional** — 5 min, every gym day.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Chest Opener + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Small to large, both directions.
**The push-day shoulder anchor — never skipped.** Full band sequence, controlled.
**LOAD:** 18lb. Inverted bell over a vertical forearm, grip hard, shoulder packed. Cuff prep.
**Kinesis, light.** Chest opener — warmup pass, not the working set.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
Elbows ~45°, pack down not up. One easy set.
**Greasing set — not to failure.** Keeps the pattern warm.
**Protective shrug.** 40-50lb pair behind the body, palms back. Blades DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s squeeze.

sets.name: Push Press (3 Sets at 45, Run First, FULL 2 Min Rest) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb DBs. 3 sets, full 2 min rest, runs first.
- **Blades DOWN and BACK into the back pockets** before the bell moves, held through lockout — traps quiet
- **Hips deliver the drive, the shoulder receives it**
- **Ribs DOWN** at the start, no arching under the weight
- 'Could do more in the end' last week — spend that on a **slower eccentric or a pause**, not more load. The pack-down is the honest ceiling

sets.name: Incline DB Press (50 — Pack-Down Is the Gate to 55) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb pair, 3 sets of 12. Keep the 2s eccentric you added last week.
- **Pack DOWN and BACK** — blades set into the bench before the first rep
- **Elbows ~45°**, full stretch at the bottom, no bounce
- **55 is available** the week the pack-down survives all twelve reps — not before

sets.name: Dips — Chest-Bias / Lean-Forward (Tempo Is the Lever; Mini-Dip Warmup First) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** bodyweight, 3 sets. Two or three mini-dips first.
- **3s eccentric** — the slow descent is the progression
- **Lean the torso forward** for the chest bias, elbows tracking back
- **Shoulders packed DOWN** at the top
- **Watch the palms** — pressure showed up last week. If it persists, adjust hand position on the bars; it's not a load or tempo problem

sets.name: 🔆 DB Lateral Raise (Spotlight — Slow It Down) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 15lb. 3 sets. 🔥

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the slow lift is the whole thing:**
- **Lead with the elbows**, pinkies slightly high
- **Slow up AND slow down** — you said you could go slower, so do; constant tension, no swinging
- **Pack DOWN** — traps quiet, the side delt does the work, not a shrug
- **Pause a beat at the top**, control back down — don't drop the weight
- Last set may go near failure once the tempo is clean

**Reflection:** can you keep the traps quiet for the whole set, or do they start doing the lifting once it burns? The delt-not-trap feeling is the win, not the rep count.

sets.name: Kinesis Cable Fly (Step Forward to Deepen) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Kinesis 9. 3 sets.
- **Step forward to deepen the stretch** — the ROM is the lever, and it's been working ('always pretty hard')
- **Soft elbows, fixed angle** — a fly, not a press
- **Squeeze at the midline**, slow return into the stretch

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Block — Tri Ext FIRST → Straight-Arm Pulldown → Lat Raise (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **70** (default), Kinesis 5 fallback. Kneeling. **Runs FIRST this week.** 🔥

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — fixed elbow, deep stretch:**
- **Elbows stay put — only the forearms move.** This is the whole lift; if the elbows drift the long head stops stretching
- **Full stretch overhead**, then lock out without flaring the ribs
- Now that it's at the FRONT (it 'got much harder' running last), judge the movement itself, not the fatigue
- Last set may go near failure

**Reflection:** does the elbow actually stay fixed through the whole set, or drop to help at the end? Fixed elbow = the stretch is honest.

**LOAD:** cable column **120** — holds, in the MIDDLE slot this week.
- **Pack the shoulders DOWN**, soft elbows at a fixed angle
- Drive the bar to the thighs with the lats, **ribs down** — no leaning back
- Slow return, full stretch overhead
- It was 'immensely easier' run first last week — the middle slot should sit fine too

**LOAD:** Kinesis 5-6 (default). Cable column 30 / pulley 10 if taken. **Runs last this week.** 🔥
- Lead with the elbow, **traps quiet**
- Constant tension — light enough to eat the tail slot fine

sets.notes: 3 rounds. Order rotated so no lift sits last two weeks running. Note which equipment you used for the lat raise.

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks — Grip Caps It)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb per hand, 3 walks, 45-60s each.
- **Shoulders packed DOWN**, ribs down, tall spine
- **Walk slow and even**, no leaning or rushing the turn
- **No straps** — the grip-limited number is the honest one
- It's a nothingburger now, and that's fine — no number needed. Just walk it clean

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow height.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress.
30s each side.
45s each side.
Slow breathing — the parasympathetic shift.

tips: **Cable block order rotates: tri ext first, straight-arm middle, cable lat raise last.** No lift dead-last two weeks running.
**Lateral raise spotlight: slow it down.** Lead with the elbow, traps quiet, delt-not-shrug.
**Tri ext spotlight: fixed elbow, deep stretch.** Only the forearm moves.
**Push press holds 45** — spend the headroom on tempo, not load.
**Incline DB holds 50** — 55 when the pack-down survives all 12.
**Farmer carry 50lb × 3 walks** — nothingburger, no number needed.
🔥 near-failure OK on lateral raise, cable lat raise, tri ext. 🛑 keep it shy on push press, incline DB, dips, fly, straight-arm, carry.
formPhilosophy: Two lifts that have coasted on 'fine' for weeks get the spotlight, because 'fine' is where quiet form debt hides — a lateral raise creeping into a shrug, a triceps extension whose elbow has started to drift. Neither needs more weight; both need attention, which is a different and cheaper thing. Meanwhile the cable block keeps rotating its order on principle: last week taught us the tail slot, not the load, was making a lift feel brutal, so the fix isn't to move a number, it's to make sure the tax lands on a different lift each week. Small corrections, held loads, the floor rising underneath. Building decades, not weeks.
